sentences: AI startup Traversal raises $120 million at $1 billion valuation.
The New York-based company is developing AI agents to diagnose software failures as businesses grapple with the growing complexity of AI-generated code.

AI startup Traversal has raised $120 million in a funding round that values the company at $1 billion, as demand grows for technology that can identify and resolve software problems created by increasingly complex AI-driven applications.
The funding round, announced Nov.
3, was co-led by Kleiner Perkins, Redpoint Ventures and Khosla Ventures, with significant participation from existing investors Sequoia Capital and Battery Ventures.
The investment will support the company’s efforts to expand its artificial intelligence platform and develop technology that can increasingly automate software troubleshooting.

Founded in 2023, Traversal develops AI agents that investigate software failures, identify their underlying causes and recommend solutions.
Its customers include major companies such as American Express, Pepsi and Blackstone, according to a Nov.
3 report by Forbes staff writer Rashi Shrivastava.
The startup’s technology addresses a growing challenge for businesses adopting AI-assisted software development.
While AI coding tools let companies develop applications and add new features faster, the resulting software can become increasingly difficult to monitor, maintain, and troubleshoot.
Traversal CEO and co-founder Anish Agarwal told Forbes that AI-generated software can fail in fundamentally different ways from traditional applications.
AI systems can appear to function normally while underlying models drift into unintended behavior.
Software updates can also pass existing tests but fail in situations developers did not anticipate.
Traversal’s AI agents analyze billions of logs and performance metrics to investigate technical problems across applications and infrastructure.
The system identifies potential causes of failures and recommends fixes, reducing the time engineers spend examining complex software systems.
The company reported that its annual recurring revenue grew ninefold over the six months preceding the funding announcement.
Its AI agents also assisted customers with more than 150,000 investigations during the previous quarter.
Agarwal did not disclose the company’s exact revenue figures, Forbes reported.
The technology has already demonstrated its potential in resolving major operational disruptions.
Agarwal described an incident at a bank where thousands of engineers were assembled in a war room to investigate why customers could not access their accounts.

The problem was traced to a database operating slowly deep within the bank’s infrastructure.
When a similar disruption occurred months later, Traversal’s AI agents completed the troubleshooting process in five minutes, Agarwal told Forbes.

Kleiner Perkins partner Mamoon Hamid said AI has increased the urgency of addressing software reliability issues, describing the situation as an emerging challenge for businesses deploying AI technologies.
Traversal’s founders include Agarwal, Raaz Dwivedi, Raj Agrawal and Ahmed Lone.

According to the company’s official website, Agarwal is a professor of operations research and computer science at Columbia University, while Dwivedi holds a similar academic position at Cornell Tech.
Both have backgrounds in machine learning research.
Agrawal holds a Ph.D. in computer science from MIT, while Lone previously worked at financial firm Citadel Securities.
The funding comes as companies increasingly invest in AI infrastructure and applications while confronting the operational challenges associated with deploying these technologies at scale.
Traversal is positioning its platform as a way to address the gap between writing software with AI and ensuring that applications continue to operate reliably after deployment.
Its latest funding will help expand its research, engineering and commercial operations as it pursues more autonomous software monitoring and troubleshooting.
